summary.headline: Sangam India Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR1,000 crore for first time at INR1,045 crore (+33% YoY), with PAT of INR53 crore, a record.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the best quarter in Sangam's history, with revenue of INR1,045 crore (+33% YoY), EBITDA of INR127 crore and PAT of INR53 crore, all record highs. H1 revenue was INR1,906 crore and H1 PAT INR94 crore, already above full-year FY26 PAT. Management reiterated the aspiration to at least double FY26 PAT in FY27, while debtor days rose to 77 from 67 in March and net debt to equity rose to 1.15x amid a INR1,500 crore capex programme. Operating cash flow was negative in the quarter, and management guided it positive by March 2027.

financial_highlights.change: Up from about 1x in prior quarters

segments.name: Synthetics (recycled polyester fibre, PV-dyed yarn, suiting fabrics)
segments.commentary: Management did not disclose segment-level figures. Polyester: about 40% sourced from in-house recycled-waste capacity, balance domestic.

segments.name: Cotton (cotton yarn, denim fabric, open-end yarn)
segments.commentary: Yarn is about 48% of revenue. Denim capacity utilisation was above 96-97% in the quarter; denim realisation about INR170-175 per metre.

segments.name: Garmenting (seamless garments, about 2% of revenue, 100% subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was 37% in Q2 vs 22% a year ago; management guided FY27 utilisation to 50-60%. Margins said to be slightly higher than group average.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated that FY27 PAT will at least double FY26 PAT (FY26 base implied at about INR83 crore from the analyst's INR166 crore doubling figure); said 'we are going to at least double our PAT'.
Expects operating cash flow to be positive by March 2027; debtor days targeted back to March levels (67 days) in H2.
Captive renewable power share: about 10% last year, about 35% now, about 50% by end FY27, stabilising at about 70% from Q1 FY28.
About INR50-55 crore of full-year EBITDA yet to accrue from renewable capacity recently commissioned or still to be commissioned.
Garmenting utilisation expected at 50-60% for full FY27.

Long-term net debt expected to peak around INR1,500 crore at end of capex cycle; comfort range for net debt to EBITDA of 3-3.5x over the long run; net debt to equity to return to about 1-1.1x over the longer term.
Promoter equity infusion of about INR100 crore; INR25 crore received in the quarter via warrant payment.
Cotton yarn capacity to rise about 60-70% from the capex underway; 40-50% of new capacity to be used captively for denim.

Capex: about 60% of the INR1,500 crore plan detailed in the investor presentation; balance plan to be firmed up over the next 2 quarters. Benefits from the larger capex expected from next financial year.
capex_capacity: INR1,500 crore capex plan over 2 to 3 years, about 60% detailed in the presentation; funding about 70-75% via debt at roughly 6-6.5% cost.

Cotton yarn project with investment of about INR600-620 crore, with expected EBITDA of about INR130 crore per analyst's figure; management did not confirm asset turnover and said EBITDA is exclusive of state subsidies.
Plants running close to full capacity; new capacity includes modernising spinning with newer machines replacing 15-20-year-old equipment.
Renewable power: captive share rising as above; about INR200 crore spent on renewable power per analyst's figure.
Operating across 8 locations in Rajasthan with over 12,000 employees.
demand_pricing: Order visibility across divisions is typically 45-60 days.
Government and institutional tenders were about INR200 crore in H1 (about 10% of revenue); management says it will not push this share materially higher, given longer receivable cycles.
Yarn is easier to pass through to customers than denim fabric; company says it is short of supply on yarn.
Company does not hedge cotton prices; cotton imports are chosen case by case on viability.
Bangladesh and Vietnam described as customers/markets rather than competitors for yarn and denim.
Export shipments are taking longer to reach customers, so exports have been more measured this year.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of the INR1,500 crore expansion and cotton yarn capacity addition in metric tons.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said firmed-up items are in the presentation; cotton yarn capacity to rise about 60-70% from capex underway. Further details to come in subsequent quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 PAT doubling guidance be reiterated, given H1 PAT of INR94 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated: 'we are going to at least double our PAT from last year in this year'; said being conservative may be better, but expects to beat.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt to equity rising to 1.15x, and how much more debt is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Elevated for a brief period due to capex funded largely by debt at about 6-6.5%; long-run target 1-1.1x; net debt to EBITDA of 3-3.5x comfortable; net debt expected to rise to about INR1,500 crore before declining.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative despite margin gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables are high (77 days) due to focus on domestic institutional tenders and elongated export shipments; expects operating cash flow positive by March and debtor days back to March level.

qa_highlights.question: Could quantum of renewable power benefit in Q2 be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still being quantified and would be shared by email post-call; the INR50-55 crore yet to accrue on a full-year basis is from capacity commissioned or to be commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Garmenting utilisation and full-year outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 utilisation 37% vs 22% last year; full-year expected at 50-60% on seasonal order pickup in H2.

risks_watch: Receivables and debtor days (77 days in September vs 67 in March); government tender exposure may lengthen cycles and need working capital; factoring or discounting being explored.
Net debt to equity at 1.15x and net debt rising towards INR1,500 crore as capex is debt-funded; interest cost of about 6-6.5%.
Negative operating cash flow in Q2; management targets positive by March 2027.
Garmenting utilisation at 37% in Q2 remains low versus the H2 target of 50-60% for the full year.
Execution risk on capex: only about 60% of the INR1,500 crore plan is firmed up; benefits expected from FY28.
Export shipment delays on longer transit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating results and the PAT-doubling aspiration, but cautious and sometimes evasive on capex returns, segment margins, yarn spreads and per-kg EBITDA, which management declined to quantify. It was candid that receivables and debtor days were a concern.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 has been the best quarter in Sangam's history.
So I think today I'm relatively confident to say that we are going to beat, we are going to at least double our PAT from last year in this year.
Operating cash flow will be positive for sure.
So, being conservative may be better, but let us see where the numbers land up.

adds.what: Cotton yarn capacity expansion of about 60-70% by quantity under the INR1,500 crore capex plan
Spinning modernisation replacing 15-20-year-old machines (part of INR1,500 crore capex plan)
Captive renewable power capacity: share of power rising from ~35% now to ~50% by end FY27 and ~70% from Q1 FY28

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 PAT at least double FY26 (base ~INR83 crore implied) with H1 PAT already INR94 crore, and Q2 revenue rose 33% YoY; backing is partial, with a cotton yarn capacity addition of ~60-70% and INR1,500 crore capex only about 60% detailed, two quarters or more from being live.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: About INR50-55 crore of full-year EBITDA yet to accrue from recently commissioned or pending renewable capacity, with captive power share rising from about 35% now to about 50% by end FY27 and about 70% from Q1 FY28; Q2 EBITDA was a record INR127 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cotton yarn capacity to rise about 60-70% from capex underway (about INR610 crore project) and spinning modernisation is under construction, but management says benefits come from next financial year, so new capacity is two or more quarters away.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Denim utilisation at 96.5% and plants running close to full capacity, with garmenting utilisation guided up from 37% in Q2 to 50-60% for FY27 on H2 seasonal order pickup.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR1,500 crore capex plan over 2-3 years is under way, but only about 60% is detailed and the balance is to be firmed up over the next 2 quarters, so further capex details are likely to be announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 PAT at least double FY26 (base about INR83 crore) with H1 PAT already INR94 crore, and said it expects to beat, though it called being conservative better.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated the PAT-doubling aspiration on H1 PAT of INR94 crore; the main risks are working capital (debtor days 77 vs 67) and negative Q2 operating cash flow rather than the earnings guide.

rows.label: Debtor days back to March levels (67 days)
rows.why: Debtor days rose to 77 from 67 and management aspires to return to 67 in H2, but it is also reliant on government tenders (about INR200 crore, about 10% of revenue) with longer receivable cycles.

rows.label: Positive operating cash flow by March 2027
rows.why: Operating cash flow was negative in Q2 with receivables elevated, and management said positive 'for sure' by March 2027.

rows.label: Net debt peaks near INR1,500 crore then falls
rows.why: Net debt to equity at 1.15x and net debt/EBITDA at 3.25x (down from 4.5x) with net debt expected to peak around INR1,500 crore at end of the capex cycle before returning to 1-1.1x equity over the longer term.

tone.note: Management was confident on record Q2 results and the PAT-doubling aspiration (reiterated with H1 PAT at INR94 crore), but cautious or evasive on capex returns, segment margins, yarn spreads and per-kg EBITDA; analysts pushed on debtor days, negative operating cash flow and debt funding.
